text.p: Individual Inc on Wednesday said it has discontinued the operations of its Freeloader unit, an Internet service it acquired one year ago.
As a result of the closing, 28 staff positions will be cut in the San Francisco and Washington D.C. offices, it said.
The company said that no adverse financial impact will come from the discontinuance, as the assets of Freeloader had previously been written off as in-process technology.
In addition, the discontinuance of the service will reduce Individual's operating expenses by about $1 million per quarter, Individual said.
Individual acquired Freeloader Inc in June 1996 for about $38 million. Freeloader's software allows users to download news and information from the Internet and view it off-line.

In February 1997, Individual said it was looking to sell the unit or draw in major investors. Individual executives told analysts then that the unsuccessful acquisition was a hindrance to the firm's drive toward profitability.

Individual also said on Wednesday it has formed an advanced technology unit to support its "Webcasting" applications, or products that automatically send personalized business news and information from the Internet to a user's screen.

The company announced the formation of a broadcast applications group, which will incorporate a small team of personnel from the former Freeloader unit, as well as people and technology from Individual.
The new group will focus on developing and distributing Individual's NewsPage products for Webcasting applications, Individual said.
Individual's corporate investors include Knight-Ridder Inc and Microsoft Corp.
